question: Refer to the exhibit. A developer must create a Bash script that performs a Chef Client reload in the event of a system reset. Which command completes the script?
context:
. /etc/init.d/functions
exec="/usr/bin/chef-client"
prog="chef-client"
[ -e /etc/sysconfig/$prog ] && . /etc/sysconfig/$prog
config=${CONFIG:-/etc/chef/client.rb}
pidfile=${PIDFILE:-/var/run/chef/client.pid}
reload() {
  echo -n $"Reloading $prog: "
  <blank>
  retval=$?
  echo
  return $retval
}
case "$1" in
  reload)
    rh_status_q || exit 7
    ;;
  exit 2
  esac
  exit $?
theory: Standard SysV-style init scripts implement a 'reload' action by sending the daemon a SIGHUP signal (not a full stop/start), so the running chef-client process re-reads its configuration in place. The killproc utility takes its pidfile argument with the '-p' flag, followed by the executable path and the signal name '-HUP' — the other option flags ('-n', '-pi') aren't valid killproc syntax for specifying the pidfile. (Cisco documentation / web research)
